newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's money market rate eases back to 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's money market rate eases back to 8.5 pct.

text.p: The weighted price of money on Croatia's money market eased back 10 basis points to 8.5 percent on Monday in thin trade due to kuna shortages.
A supply shrinkage caused total settlements to fall to 26.3 million kuna from Monday's 127 million. Borrowers had sought 44 million, dealers said.
Interbank call money at 8.0 percent, compared to 7.0 last week, made up two thirds of the 25.4 million kuna new loans.
Bank creditors rolled over old one-week to two-month placements at firmer 10.2-18 percent rates.
Insurers charged a steady 7.0 percent for renewed one-week deals.

The central bank's kuna midrates for Wednesday eased to 6.5463 from 6.4502 against the dollar and to 3.5626 versus 3.5616 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
